headings.text: 3.1 Assignment simplex, expert loads, and affinity

extracts.text: Consider M M routed items, each associated with a gradient observation. An item is a unit of training data with one routing distribution and one gradient observation: a token, an example, or, in all our experiments, a same-task group of up to eight training examples with group-averaged routing probabilities (Section 5.2 ). The router assigns each item to a distribution over K K experts, giving

Let W ∈ ℝ M × M W\in\mathbb{R}^{M\times M} be a symmetric affinity matrix, where W i ​ j W_{ij} is large when routed items i i and j j induce similar gradient directions and small or negative when their gradients conflict; Section 3.3 instantiates it from gradients. Together, P P and W W determine how much similarity mass each expert collects, Q ⁡ ( P , W ) := P ⊤ ​ W ​ P ∈ ℝ K × K Q(P;W):=P^{\top}WP\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times K} , whose diagonal entry Q k ​ k Q_{kk} is the affinity mass assigned to surrogate group k k . Under the gradient Gram instantiation below, it measures the squared norm of an aggregate in a common parameter template, rather than the actual update to physical expert k k .

The unnormalized affinity Q k ​ k Q_{kk} grows with both gradient agreement and the number of assigned observations. Dividing by assigned mass separates the per-observation reward from this quadratic load scaling. Summing over experts gives the load-normalized association
